title: A heap and a deque
description:
Write two functions with the right collections:

- `fn smallest_k(nums: &[i64], k: usize) -> Vec<i64>`: the `k` smallest numbers in increasing order, using a `BinaryHeap` (of at most `k` items) rather than sorting everything.
- `fn sliding_max(nums: &[i64], window: usize) -> Vec<i64>`: the largest number in each window of `window` neighbouring numbers, using a `VecDeque` of indexes so each number is pushed and popped at most once. A window of 0 or bigger than the slice gives an empty `Vec`.

```rust
smallest_k(&[5, 1, 9, 3, 7], 3)          // [1, 3, 5]
sliding_max(&[1, 3, -1, -3, 5, 3, 6], 3)   // [3, 3, 5, 5, 6]
```
hints: A max-heap that never holds more than `k` items keeps the `k` smallest: when it grows past `k`, `pop()` throws out the largest. `into_sorted_vec()` gives them in increasing order (lesson 8.03).
For the sliding maximum, keep indexes in the deque with decreasing values: before pushing `i`, pop from the back every index whose value is not bigger; the front is always the window's maximum.
